newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle end off ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle end off ahead of report.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower ahead of the monthly USDA Cattle-on-feed report as long liquidation prompted by easier cash markets weighed on prices, traders said.
Live cattle ended 0.550 to 0.075 lower with October off most at 71.950 cents. Feeder cattle finished unchanged to 0.250 cent lower with October off 0.250 at 63.700 cents.

Long liquidation developed on declining cash beef prices and easing of packer bids with futures slipping into early sell stops. Packers lowered fed cattle bids to $71 per cwt. Evening up ahead of the report was also cited, trades said.

Unwinding of bull spreads ahead of the monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report continued despite expectations the report will show fed cattle supplies under year ago levels. Placements may be up and on-feed supplies rising somewhat but fed supplies are still less than last year, they said.

Projections on the report for on-feed cattle supplies as of September 1 in the seven key states averaged 89.9 percent and ranged from 88.2 to 92 percent of a year ago. The number of cattle placed in feedlots averaged 112.7 percent in a range of 106.6 to 119 percent, and marketings averaged 94.7 in a range of 92 to 98 percent of a year ago.

Refco, R.J. O'Brien, LIT division of First Options, Rosenthal Collins and RBH sold October early. In live cattle options, there was active selling of December 66 puts and February 62 puts and buying of October 71 and 72 puts early, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of live cattle ahead of the report with higher corn futures also overhanging the market, traders said.
ADM Investor Services, Chicago Corp and Stone Traders sold October early with locals weighing on prices in later action, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.07 at $64.20 per cwt, highest since December 27.
